Meet Dr. Nicole Apelian: A Lifetime Dedicated to Natural Healing

To understand the value behind the Medicinal Seed Kit, it helps to understand the person who put it together. Dr. Nicole Apelian graduated with a degree in Biology from McGill University and further sharpened her deep botanical skills while living for years in the Kalahari Desert alongside one of the oldest cultures on Earth, the San Bushmen. Observing how these indigenous people lived long, vibrant lives free from commercial pills left a lasting impression.

Later in life, Nicole faced a severe personal health challenge when she was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) at just 29 years old. Left largely confined to a wheelchair by chronic agony and conventional treatments that offered little relief, she decided to take matters into her own hands. By turning to natural remedies grown personally in her yard, she reclaimed her vitality—so much so that she successfully survived for 57 days straight out in the brutal wild on the TV show Alone without modern luxuries or medicine.

Her personal journey from wheelchair-bound patient to thriving wilderness survivor inspired her to create the Medicinal Seed Kit. Her mission is simple: to empower everyday families to take control of their health, embrace self-reliance, and unlock the healing power growing right outside their back doors.

The 10 Essential Medicinal Plants You Will Grow

Each plant featured in the kit was hand-selected for its unique medicinal properties, ease of growth, and incredible historical utility. Let’s take a closer look at the 10 powerhouse plants included in your garden:

1. Chicory (The Painkilling Plant)

Valued historically by Native Americans for soothing physical discomforts and stiff joints, chicory root is rich in chicoric acid—a natural compound with powerful anti-inflammatory and analgesic qualities without the risk of addiction.

2. Yarrow (The Wound Healer)

Famously used by Dr. Apelian on day 42 of Alone to stop a severe hand wound from bleeding in minutes, yarrow is an exceptional natural antiseptic and clotting agent that helps prevent infection.

3. California Poppy (Natural Sleep Support)

An incredible natural alternative to addictive prescription sleeping pills. Brewing a gentle sleep tea or a concentrated tincture supports deep, uninterrupted, and restorative eight-hour sleep cycles.

4. Marshmallow (Digestive Health Soother)

Packed with a natural mucilage sap, marshmallow root and leaves coat and protect the stomach, intestines, and colon, offering natural relief from heartburn, acid reflux, indigestion, and minor tummy upsets.

5. Chamomile (The Gardener's Doctor)

A true traditional heal-all. Chamomile flowers make a calming tea that eases digestive muscles, helps relax the body, and creates soothing compresses for tired or irritated eyes and skin.

6. Evening Primrose (Skin & Nerve Support)

Opening exclusively at sunset, evening primrose provides essential gamma-linolenic and linolenic acids required by skin and nerve cell membranes, offering wonderful topical support for skin health and nerve comfort.

7. Lavender (Anti-Inflammatory & Calmative)

Beyond its wonderful fragrance and ability to repel household pests, lavender oil has been shown in clinical studies to significantly reduce everyday anxiety levels and support balanced mood recovery.

8. Echinacea (Immune System Defender)

Because commercial supplements found in stores are frequently heavily counterfeited or watered down, growing your own organic echinacea ensures you have a potent, pure immune booster ready at the first sign of a cold.

9. Calendula (Skin Repair & Lymphatic Cleanser)

A favorite of traditional herbalists for soothing minor scrapes, cuts, burns, and skin rashes. When enjoyed as a tea, calendula also gently supports the cleansing of the lymphatic system.

10. Feverfew (Nature's Aspirin)

A potent anti-inflammatory herb traditionally used by herbalists to help manage fevers, soothe throbbing tension headaches, and bring comfort to achy joints and muscles.
